An under-trained low-LR net is further held back by weight pull.
Depth supplies the expressivity that narrow layers lack.
Strong L2 shrinks weights in every layer and compounds multiplicatively with depth, hurting signal propagation.
Deep stacks amplify step errors and sit closer to the stability cliff at large LR.
A single hidden layer's only capacity route is width, so widening helps most there.
Wider layers move the function more per step, so large LRs diverge sooner.

Shallow nets tolerate large steps and are often under-trained at low LR.
